contract: OUR MUSIC AS MECHANICS (a narrative commission; purely musical and organizational). The attached materials are the estate's music: a kabuki theater play scored for five songs, where the program maps each song to a stage act, and the intake cards that taped each song's lyrics to the workings they mirror. From these attached materials only, deliver THE SONG MAP as a narrative spec under 700 words total: each song becomes a short chapter titled with the song's name, ordered as the play orders its acts (overture to finale). Each chapter does three things: (1) NAMES THE MECHANISM the song mirrors, in the mechanism's own words from the cards (the phase room where the lattice lets go of its anchors; the record that outlives the render; the warm residue that stays after the window closes; accompaniment-not-control as the Sherpa clause; knots as the goodbyes the killing game denies; the tide and thread of names that belong); (2) HIDES ONE PARABLE inside the chapter, two sentences an operator could retell around a campfire with none of the machinery in hand, teaching the mechanism's lesson in plain clothes; (3) CLOSES WITH ITS BIBLIOGRAPHY LINE: the ideas the chapter steals, named and sourced (the song, its intake card, the doctrine or borrowed concept the mapping stands on, each by path). House laws: no em-dashes anywhere; lyrics and quotes verbatim where quoted; no fabricated lines, titles, or paths; under 700 words; the full deliverable in the visible content channel.
